title: Daemon host repository and scope catalog authority
description: Objective: create the missing server-owned resolver from durable project repository/scope identities to host workspace configuration. MEASURED at HEAD f81ab75: RepositoryObservation stores opaque repositoryRef/scopeRef, GraphNode has no scopes, project configuration is path-neutral, and no production resolver exists. Deliverable: publish the existing structural snapshotProjectState validator from @moe/core and add a bounded, versioned, digest-sealed daemon-startup catalog authority mapping exact (projectId, repositoryRef, scopeRef) to sourceRepositoryRoot, worktreeParent, and sorted canonical repository-relative declared paths. The authority reads current durable ProjectState itself and applies the approved rule that the final RepositoryObservation is current; it accepts no observation, cwd, root, or paths from a command payload. NOT in scope: creating/removing worktrees, reading workspace bytes, result scanning, provider launch, or changing project.bind_repository wire shape. Owned paths: packages/core/src/index.ts, packages/core/src/index-surface.test.ts, apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-repository-scope-authority.ts/.js/.test.ts. Consumer: the prepare-before-launch lifecycle task created by this split; its exact task id must be recorded before completion. Verification command (PowerShell, one foreground gate with separately recorded legs): `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck; $a=$LASTEXITCODE; pnpm --filter @moe/core test; $b=$LASTEXITCODE; pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck; $c=$LASTEXITCODE; pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test; $d=$LASTEXITCODE; Write-Host "CORE_TC=$a CORE_TEST=$b DAEMON_TC=$c DAEMON_TEST=$d"; if ($a -ne 0 -or $b -ne 0 -or $c -ne 0 -or $d -ne 0) { exit 1 }` and both test legs must print nonzero counts.
definitionOfDone: The @moe/core bare root publishes snapshotProjectState with its curated surface ratchet intact; apps/daemon already declares @moe/core and pnpm-lock carries the importer edge, and a temporary compiled daemon probe imports the bare specifier, typechecks exit 0, and is deleted in the same command.

A closed, bounded catalog codec admits exactly one versioned field set, canonicalizes and sorts repository-relative scope paths, validates host roots/worktree parents without shell normalization, derives a digest over every admitted field, and refuses malformed, duplicate, over-limit, case-colliding, absolute/UNC/device, or accessor input with exact stable code and layer.

Resolution reads and structurally snapshots the durable ProjectState for the bound project, selects only its final RepositoryObservation as current, and exact-matches projectId, repositoryRef, scopeRef, baseRevisionHash, and a catalog entry; absent, ambiguous, unreadable, stale, or mismatched facts refuse distinctly with no fallback.

The returned frozen authority contains only catalog-owned sourceRepositoryRoot, worktreeParent, canonical declared paths, catalog digest, and durable logical/base identities; request cwd/paths, NodeMission.workspace, launchTemplate, and Git changed paths are unrepresentable as inputs.

Focused tests use a real SqliteEventStore accepted control plus a nonzero generated hostile roster and assert every refusal code and refusing layer; mutating production to trust the first repository observation or a caller path reddens named production-surface tests.
The exact production consumer task id is recorded before completion, core and daemon typecheck/test legs each exit 0, and both test legs print nonzero Test Files/Tests counts.
taskRails: The daemon-startup catalog is the sole logical-ref-to-host-path authority for this M1 slice; commands may identify durable refs but may never supply or override physical roots or declared paths.
The final RepositoryObservation is current by explicit product decision for this append-only M1 state; do not silently select an older match or merge observations.
Do not reimplement project-state validation in the daemon: use the public @moe/core snapshotProjectState production surface and verify the manifest/lock/bare-import edge.
No filesystem mutation, worktree creation, provider launch, or caller fallback belongs in this task; fail closed with stable code/layer and commit explicit owned paths only.

(a) CODEC. One versioned field set; entries sorted by the whole (projectId, repositoryRef, scopeRef) key so the digest is a function of the admitted SET rather than of operator file order; declaredPaths sorted then case-folded for collision; results deep-frozen (catalog, entries array, each entry, each declaredPaths array). The digest preimage folds catalogVersion in FROM THE CATALOG, not from the constant, so a tampered version moves the digest instead of surviving it. Host-root fence admits exactly two spellings — `^[A-Za-z]:\` with backslashes, or rooted POSIX with forward slashes — and refuses `\\?\`, `\\.\`, UNC, drive-relative `C:x`, bare `C:`, mixed separators, trailing separator, dot/parent segments, reserved device stems, trailing dot/space, non-NFC and non-well-formed WITHOUT calling path.normalize or any shell.

(b) RESOLUTION. Reads durable state through the PRODUCTION readers `readDurableLedger(store, projectId)` then `stateOf(ledger, projectId)` (aggregateIdFor pins project aggregates to the bare projectId — bootstrap-sequence.ts:43-48, verified), then RE-VALIDATES the raw JsonValue through the newly published `snapshotProjectState` from the @moe/core BARE specifier. Current-rule: `state.repositoryObservations[length - 1]`, the FINAL entry, per the approved product decision. Exact-matches state.projectId, and the current observation's repositoryRef, scopeRef and baseRevisionHash, each on its own line with its own code, then looks up the catalog entry for the exact triple. Catalog digest is RECOMPUTED and compared before any store read, so a tampered decoded catalog cannot resolve.

PAYLOAD INDEPENDENCE BY CONSTRUCTION: `FoundationRepositoryScopeRequest` has exactly four fields and all four are durable identity refs. A cwd, worktreeRoot, declaredPaths, NodeMission.workspace, launchTemplate or Git changed-path list is not a field that exists to be rejected — and `ownValues(request, REQUEST_KEYS)` refuses any extra key with REQUEST_MALFORMED@RESOLUTION, so the runtime agrees with the type.

ONE ADDED CODE beyond the plan's enumeration: FOUNDATION_REPOSITORY_SCOPE_PROJECT_STATE_UNREADABLE. DoD 3 lists "absent, ambiguous, unreadable, stale, or mismatched" as refusing DISTINCTLY; a store read that throws (closed handle) is not an absent project, and folding it into PROJECT_STATE_ABSENT would make a broken store indistinguishable from an unregistered project. Mapping of the DoD's five words onto the vocabulary: absent -> PROJECT_STATE_ABSENT / OBSERVATION_ABSENT / ENTRY_ABSENT; unreadable -> PROJECT_STATE_UNREADABLE (throwing store) and PROJECT_STATE_INVALID (bytes snapshotProjectState refuses); stale -> BASE_REVISION_MISMATCH; mismatched -> PROJECT/REPOSITORY/SCOPE_MISMATCH; ambiguous -> ENTRY_DUPLICATE at catalog admission (durable observations are NOT ambiguous — the final one is current by decision).

Instead each resolution arm gets a targeted mutation drill in step 6 — delete or invert the guard, confirm the NAMED test reddens, restore — which is the check epic rail 6 actually asks for and is strictly stronger than assertion ordering.

CONTROL IS A REAL STORE. `SqliteEventStore.openEphemeralForProjectTest` via the shared bootstrap fixtures, driven by the PRODUCTION command path (`runBootstrapCommand` behind `send`) for project.register and project.bind_repository — no stubbed ledger reader anywhere. `bindOnto` reads the current version through `versionOf(readDurableLedger(...))` so a second bind is a real durable append rather than a hand-set number. ARMS, each asserting the [code, layer] TUPLE against DAEMON_REPOSITORY_SCOPE_RESOLUTION:
- PROJECT_STATE_ABSENT — store with no register.
- PROJECT_STATE_UNREADABLE — bound store then `store.close()`; proves a broken store is UNKNOWN, not an absent project.
- PROJECT_STATE_INVALID — committed bytes snapshotProjectState refuses (`{lifecycle, repositoryObservations}` only). This is the arm that pays for step 1: without the re-validation the resolver would read `.repositoryObservations` straight off corrupt bytes and ACCEPT.
- OBSERVATION_ABSENT — registered, never bound (honest, no plant).
- PROJECT_MISMATCH — valid ProjectState naming project-2 filed under the project-1 aggregate.
- REPOSITORY_MISMATCH / SCOPE_MISMATCH / BASE_REVISION_MISMATCH — a 3-row table, count pinned at 3, ONE field varied per row, and the catalog deliberately carries entries for the varied refs too so ENTRY_ABSENT cannot be what answers.
- ENTRY_ABSENT — durable identity current, catalog carries only scope-elsewhere.
- CATALOG_DIGEST_MISMATCH — a decoded catalog whose entry sourceRepositoryRoot was swapped after sealing, against an ACCEPTED store so nothing else can answer first.
- REQUEST_MALFORMED — null, a missing field, a non-string ref, plus an 8-row roster of smuggled host facts (changedPaths, cwd, declaredPaths, launchTemplate, sourceRepositoryRoot, workspace, worktreeParent, worktreeRoot) with a positive count assertion.

CURRENT-RULE, the load-bearing one for the approved decision: two real binds; the FINAL (repo-2, scope-2) resolves ACCEPTED and the SUPERSEDED first bind — still present in the durable array and still carrying its OWN catalog entry — refuses REPOSITORY_MISMATCH. An implementation reading observations[0] flips both halves.

DETERMINISM: two resolutions over the same store and catalog are byte-identical by JSON.stringify. BOUNDED READ: 1_200 superseded observations plus the current one still resolve.

D7 case-collision guard -> "refuses two declared paths that a case-folding filesystem cannot tell apart". D8 duplicate-key guard -> "refuses a second entry under an identical (project, repository, scope) key". D9 accessor descriptor check weakened to `descriptor === undefined` -> "reads its own data descriptors once, so an accessor cannot answer twice". D10 unreadable-store catch removed -> "refuses an unreadable store as UNKNOWN rather than as an absent project". D11 host-root fence weakened to a plain ref check -> "refuses every hostile host root on BOTH root fields". D12 declared-path backslash rule removed -> "refuses every hostile declared path under one stable code". D14 trio loses its RACE arm -> "generates a positive, three-armed case count for FOUNDATION_REPOSITORY_SCOPE_LAYERS" AND the ratchet's "names every roster entry missing an arm".

ONE DRILL REDDENED FOR THE WRONG REASON AND WAS REPLACED. Unregistering `...repositoryScopeCases` made `tsc -p tests/security/tsconfig.json` fail on the now-unused binding, so the lane died before a single case ran — a red that proves nothing about coverage. Retargeted to a type-valid mutant (`.filter((c) => c.arm !== "RACE")`), which reddens the three-armed assertion BY NAME.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, and it found two real holes. Both are now closed, tested, and drilled (D15-D17, all EXIT=1, RESTORED=True):
1. AMBIGUITY AT SELECTION. Resolution used `entries.find(...)`. The codec refuses a duplicate triple, but `resolveFoundationRepositoryScope` accepts ANY value of the catalog TYPE, and `digestOf` is published — so a catalog assembled without the codec can carry the triple twice AND carry a genuine seal. `find` would have silently taken the first and let the later entry lose. Now `filter`, and `matches.length > 1` refuses ENTRY_DUPLICATE at the RESOLUTION layer (same code, different layer — which is exactly why the layer field exists). Drill D15 -> RED "refuses an uncodec'd catalog that carries the requested triple twice".
2. THE SEAL PROVES CONSISTENCY, NOT CANONICALITY. The same hand-assembled-and-resealed catalog could have carried a UNC root or a `..` path and resolution would have handed it straight back, because only the codec ran the fences. The selected entry is now RE-FENCED at the point of return through the same `isHostRoot`/`isDeclaredPath` production predicates, refusing HOST_ROOT_INVALID / PATH_NONCANONICAL at the RESOLUTION layer. That makes DoD 4's "canonical declared paths" true by construction rather than by trusting the caller's provenance. Drills D16/D17 -> RED on the two named tests. All three new tests reseal through the PUBLISHED `digestOf` and assert `digestOf(catalog) === catalog.digest` first, so the seal check provably is not what answers.
Checklist items considered and NOT changed, recorded so QA sees they were weighed: (a) concurrency — the module mutates nothing and opens no handle; a peer appending a bind between the ledger page reads can only make the resolver see the OLDER state, which fails closed as REPOSITORY_MISMATCH, never as a stale root accepted as current. (b) `Object.keys` in `ownValues` materializes keys before the arity check, so a 10M-key object buys one walk; left as-is deliberately to match the accepted precedent at foundation-attempt-codec.ts `exactKeys`, and both inputs
